More important than what a few leaders choose or fail to do, is the will of the user base.

It's been made clear by the evolution of social media is that the people go where they can get what they want.

If the waters of one site get too polluted with censorship, injected content or other bullshit, the people will seek fresher content elsewhere.

The longevity and prosperity of a social media site will always be relative to its fulfillment of its users desires. Both in quality and quantity. Those who try to game and optimize these communities only weaken the very integrity they hope to profit by.

The longest lived site will be one which has a strong starting offering, which adapts over time in lockstep with the changing tastes, fashions and memes of the time. And this only if that adaptation is driven by transparency and democratic community participation.

This is not so much a tall order on paper. In reality it goes against human nature. Any system that can be gamed will be gamed.

And so at best these sites can hope only to be administrated for as long as possible by good people aware of their own human weaknesses and with an ear for the people. Directed by their desire to provide for others, over their desire for personal profit.
